To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cumulative accuracy of a stereotactic system is the sum of all individual accuracy contributions, and that the cumulative accuracy can be calculated by linear error propagation.
the accuracy of a stereotactic system can be described by the following equation: accuracy = 0.5 × slice thickness + 0.5 mm.

the application accuracy of frame-based biopsy can be calculated by a Gaussian approach, that the accuracy is determined by a combination of several error sources, and that the accuracy is strongly influenced by the pixel size, the slice thickness and the mechanical parameters of the stereotactic frame.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general approach for calculating the cumulative accuracy of stereotaxic systems.
a general approach for calculating the accuracy of stereoscopic systems.
the development of a Gaussian approach to calculate the accuracy of stereocatic systems, including the frame-based biopsy, and the comparison of the results with measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accuracy of the frame-based stereotactic biopsy is determined by the imaging accuracy, the image to frame registration error, the frame accuracy, and the mechanical parameters of the stereotactic system.

for frame-based applications the accuracy relevant for the application is determined by the slice thickness of the imaging modality used, which should not exceed 0.5–1.0 mm, and that the accuracy of frame devices can be calculated with the Gaussian approach.
the Gaussian approach is a valuable tool for a quantitative assessment of the application accuracy for stereotactic systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy of the application of stereotactic devices can be calculated with the Gaussian approach.
the accuracy of the frame devices investigated is in the range of a few millimeters.
the Gaussian approach provides a powerful tool for the prediction of frame system accuracies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the application accuracy of a stereotactic system is not only dependent on the accuracy of the imaging system but also on the accuracy of target and entry point identification, image to frame registration, and mechanical accuracy of the frame.
the Gaussian approach can serve as a general tool to predict the accuracy relevant for stereotactic applications, and to optimize the accuracy for a given frame system.
the application accuracy of frame-based stereotaxy can be predicted analytically by the Gaussian approach.
